title: feat(lint)!: membership key declarations, and the row policies that read them, are judged when authored
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoJLr1A7TYy1k6cGE23eo9VQ)_
Closes #25234
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: narrowed

PR 3 of 3 of ruling A on #25234 (ruling 6355640929, design 6344270438, landing plan 6370632236): the authoring refusals. PR 1 (#25513) declared `ObjectSchema.membershipKeys`; PR 2 (#25528) stages them per request, and every miss fails closed. This PR refuses, where the metadata is written, the declarations that cannot resolve and the policies that read a key in a way that matches no rows: refusals 4 to 7 and 11 to 13 of the design table, plus refusal 3 at the save door, and the runtime-gate registration for `object` writes.

## Refusals

| # | What | Rule id | CLI | Save door |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 3 | one key declared on two objects | `membership-key-declared-twice` | yes (`defineStack` already refuses it in one stack) | yes, reading the live objects the written stack does not carry, outside the package closure too |
| 4 | a key the registered resolver also owns | `membership-key-resolver-collision` | not judged (no resolver visible) | yes |
| 5 | `userField` missing, or not a single-valued user reference (`user`, or `lookup` / `master_detail` to `sys_user`, not `multiple`) | `membership-key-user-field-invalid` | yes | yes |
| 6 | `valueField` missing, or not a reference (`lookup`, `master_detail`, `user`) | `membership-key-value-field-invalid` | yes | yes |
| 7 | a key's `filter` that does not lower, names a column the roster lacks, compares with a list-holding column, is refused by the engine's judge, or reads any `current_user` value | the existing `rls-predicate-*` ids, at `objects[N].membershipKeys.KEY.filter` | yes | yes |
| 11 | a declared key tested against a column whose values can never be the key's (`buyer in current_user.portal_supplier_ids`) | new `rls-predicate-membership-key-target` | yes | yes |
| 12 | `x in current_user.KEY` that no kernel key, declaration or registered resolver owns | `rls-predicate-unknown-user-variable` | unchanged, `unknowable` | yes |
| 13 | a declared key under `==` | `rls-predicate-unenforceable` (the kernel list-key type fault) | yes | yes |

Refusals 5 and 6 judge the roster object as merged with its extensions (`objectExtensions`, by priority). A column two packages write at the deciding priority is left unjudged. Refusal 11 reads the key's target from the declaration's `valueField` reference, only when exactly one object declares the key. It accepts the column that references that target, and `id` on the target object itself.

## The save door

- `validateMembershipKeyDeclarations` is a new gating rule, `CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['object']`.
- `validateRlsPredicateEnforceability` now declares `runtimeTypes: ['permission', 'object']`. On an object write it judges the object's key filters and `defaultRowScope`. Through the differential gate, it also refuses an object write that drops a field or a key a stored policy reads. A stored policy that already failed is not blamed on the write.
- **The host fact.** `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` reads the registered resolver's `keys` per publish from `RLS_MEMBERSHIP_RESOLVER_SERVICE`, `[]` when none is registered (`protocol.ts#rlsMembershipResolverKeys`). `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` takes them as `rlsMembershipResolverKeys` and hands the rules a `membershipKeyOwners` context: the resolver's keys, and which live objects declare which key. The declarations are read from the un-narrowed `context.objects`, so the package closure cannot hide a key. The written stack is authoritative for the objects it carries. With no service registry, or a resolver whose `keys` is not a list of strings, no ownership is judged, as on the CLI.

## `os explain`

New entries for the four `membership-key-*` ids and `rls-predicate-membership-key-target`. Each says how a key resolves and that every miss fails closed. `rls-predicate-unenforceable` names the filter path. `rls-predicate-unknown-user-variable` gains three paragraphs: a declared key under `==`; the CLI-versus-save-door split for an unowned key in a membership position; and the caller-free filter. All verdicts and hints are one line of at most 200 characters (pinned).

## Pins moved, each with its reason in the diff

- `runtime-gate.object-writes.test.ts`: the object-door roster and the clean-write `rulesRun` gain the two rules, as ruled joins.
- `validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.engine-judge.test.ts`: `runtimeTypes` is `['permission', 'object']`.
- `validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.test.ts`: the `os explain` text the verdict moved to now says "not reported by `os validate`" where it said "never reported", because the save door now reports it.
- `packages/cli/test/rls-policy-authoring-admission.test.ts` (real `ObjectQL` host): the app-staged `current_user.holidays` cases register a resolver owning `holidays`, which is how an app stages a key. A new case pins refusal 12 end to end: with no resolver, the CLI accepts and the save door answers 422 with `rls-predicate-unknown-user-variable`.

## Tests

- `validate-membership-key-declarations.test.ts`: 17, refusals 3 to 6, both doors, merged-object judging, an unjudged priority tie, `os explain`, verdict length.
- `validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.membership-keys.test.ts`: 24, refusals 7, 11, 12 and 13, each with a CONTROL, both doors, the object write that drops a key a stored policy reads (refused) or keeps it (published), `os explain`, verdict length.
- `protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts`: 4 host cases. No resolver: refused, nothing written. A resolver owning the key: published. A resolver owning other keys: refused. No registry, a resolver without `keys`, or non-string `keys`: published.

**Ablations, each restored byte-identically from a saved copy:**

- Refusal 12 arm off: 3 red. Refusal 11 arm off: 7 red. Refusal 13 swap off: 2 red. Refusal 7 caller-read check off: 1 red. Refusal 7 judge pass off: 6 red. Stack authority over the stored declarations off: 1 red.
- Each of the six `findings.push` sites in the declarations rule disabled in turn: 1, 6, 2, 1, 4 and 3 red.
- The host's resolver read replaced by `undefined`: the two refusing host cases red, the two publishing ones green.

**Suites:**

- `@objectstack/lint`: 158 files, 7237 passed. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0. dts build with `OS_SKIP_DTS` unset: 6/6 declaration files.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: 261 files, 21457 passed, 19 skipped, before the 4 host cases; those 4 pass. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0.
- `@objectstack/cli` `rls-policy-authoring-admission.test.ts`: 40 passed.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives 71 families on this head (1,972 changed lines, under the human-merge threshold). All 71 were run one at a time under `os-verify-lock.sh`, exit codes captured before any pipe, after a dts build of the `@objectstack/cli` closure; so were 58 more the longer listing names. All exit 0 but the following.

- One real finding, fixed in `d16c4a71`: `check:docs-transcript-drift` found four docs transcripts printing "author-time rules (51)". The `validate` registry now derives 52 (the declarations rule), so the four lines read 52.
- Four are PR-context guards that judge nothing locally (exit 1 or 2 with "NOT WIRED" / "NOT MEASURED"): `check-closing-target-claim`, `check-partof-closing-keyword`, `check-single-claim-paths` and `check-governed-queue-guard`. CI runs them with the PR. `check-partof-closing-keyword` was also run with this body as `PR_BODY` and passes.

**Changeset** `.changeset/25234-membership-key-authoring-refusals.md`: `minor` on `@objectstack/lint`, `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, BREAKING with FROM, TO, Unchanged and Remedy, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. `pnpm check:adr-0087-registration` passes.
